name: schroeppel_shamir_orthogonal_vectors
description: Nederlof and Wegrzycki (STOC 2021) give the first improvement over the space complexity of the 40-year-old Schroeppel-Shamir Subset Sum algorithm while keeping the same O*(2^{n/2}) time. They reduce worst-case n-integer Subset Sum to the Orthogonal Vectors (OV) problem in a space-efficient way, and design a new OV algorithm for the hard support-size d/4 regime. The reduction combines the Schroeppel-Shamir four-way-split priority-queue method with the Howgrave-Graham-Joux representation technique (a random-prime modular filter), while the OV algorithm refines the representative-families framework of Fomin-Lokshtanov-Panolan-Saurabh. The resulting randomized algorithm runs in O*(2^{0.5n}) time and O*(2^{0.249999n}) space, improving Schroeppel-Shamir's O*(2^{n/4}) space. The construction exposes a tight two-way relation between Subset Sum and OV: any improvement of the OV algorithm would immediately improve the Subset Sum running time, which remains the long-standing open barrier.
worst_case_time: O*(2^{0.5n}) = O*(2^{n/2}); the Schroeppel-Shamir time bound is matched, not beaten.
space_complexity: O*(2^{0.249999n}), improving the previous O*(2^{n/4}) = O*(2^{0.25n}) of Schroeppel-Shamir; later improved to O*(2^{0.246n}) by Belova-Chukhin-Kulikov-Mihajlin (ESA 2024).
model: Word RAM / circuit RAM with unit-cost integer operations. [uncertain: the abstract does not name the model explicitly; the O* framing accommodates standard RAM]. The OV algorithm operates on N vectors in {0,1}^d.
randomized_or_deterministic: Randomized (Monte Carlo) with one-sided error (no false positives); success probability is high and can be amplified by repetition.
time_space_tradeoff_curve: The result is a single point at time O*(2^{0.5n}), space O*(2^{0.249999n}). Context: Schroeppel-Shamir gives a general tradeoff with space S and time about 2^n / S^2 for S <= O*(2^{n/4}); this work improves the low-space endpoint at S = 2^{0.249999n}. The tight SS-OV relation means an improvement of the OV algorithm would improve either the time or the space of this tradeoff.
numerical_exponent_and_record_year: Time exponent 0.5 (2^{0.5n}) remains unbeaten since Schroeppel-Shamir (FOCS 1979 / SIAM 1981); space exponent improved from 0.25 to 0.249999 in 2021 (STOC 2021), then to 0.246 in 2024.
problem_variant: Vanilla worst-case Subset Sum (n-integer decision/search), equivalent to Partition; the reduction targets the general worst-case instance rather than a promised/dense variant.
applies_to: Exact worst-case n-integer Subset Sum instances, including dense instances; the algorithmic core is a reduction to the Orthogonal Vectors problem on {0,1}^d vectors of support size d/4.
coefficient_set: Not a balancing/coefficient-set result: it concerns {0,1} subset selection (the indicator vector). In Subset Balancing notation this is C = [±1] (Partition/Subset Sum).
density_regime: Arbitrary worst-case / dense instances; no density restriction, and no average-case or low-density assumption.
solution_regime: General decision regime for worst-case instances; no pigeonhole/numerous-solutions promise.
key_technique: A space-efficient reduction from Subset Sum to Orthogonal Vectors (OV), obtained by merging the Schroeppel-Shamir four-way split / heap-generated pair-sums method with the Howgrave-Graham-Joux representation technique (modular filtering by a random prime); plus a new OV algorithm for N vectors in {0,1}^d with support size d/4 running in O~(N * 2^d / binom(d, d/4)), based on and refining the representative-families framework.
core_idea: Schroeppel-Shamir achieve O*(2^{n/4}) space by splitting into four lists and lazily generating pair sums with priority queues, avoiding materializing 2^{n/2} sums. Nederlof-Wegrzycki keep the 2^{n/2} time but replace the memory bottleneck with a space-efficient OV reduction: the representation technique filters candidate vectors modulo a random prime so only O*(2^{0.249999n}) objects need to be stored, and a specialized OV algorithm resolves the remaining matching step. Because the reduction is essentially lossless, Subset Sum and OV become tightly linked: improving the OV subroutine improves Subset Sum.
reduction_pipeline: Subset Sum -> Orthogonal Vectors (OV) with vectors in {0,1}^d of support size d/4; OV solved via representative families. The reduction itself uses the Schroeppel-Shamir method plus the representation technique (Howgrave-Graham-Joux).
search_vs_decision_witness: Returns an explicit witness (a subset / orthogonal pair); constructivity is proved.
obstacle_to_2n3: The time exponent stays exactly 0.5; only the space exponent is reduced. The new OV algorithm does not beat the 2^{n/2} time barrier for Subset Sum and the reduction provides no route to O*(2^{n/3}). The support-size d/4 OV regime is the hard case, and the representative-families machinery currently yields no sub-2^{0.5n} SS time. The paper itself poses beating the 2^{n/2} time as the open problem, unaffected by this space improvement.
potential_to_break_mitm: Low for the time barrier: this line improves space, not time. It could contribute indirectly because any improved OV algorithm would improve Subset Sum time, but no such OV improvement is known and the tight relation cuts both ways (an OV lower bound would obstruct progress).
barrier_evidence: The O*(2^{n/2}) time bound for Subset Sum is long-standing and unbeaten. The reduction yields a tight relation: any improvement to the OV algorithm implies an improvement over Schroeppel-Shamir's runtime, so progress is gated on restricted-OV progress. No proven unconditional lower bound forbids beating 2^{n/2}; the MITM conjecture remains open. (Subsequent work only improved space to 2^{0.246n}, confirming the time barrier's persistence.)
open_questions: (1) Design a faster algorithm for OV (support size d/4) - this would immediately improve Subset Sum time. (2) Improve the space bound further below O*(2^{0.249999n}) / O*(2^{0.246n}). (3) Obtain a O*(2^{(0.5-eps)n}) worst-case Subset Sum algorithm. (4) Characterize the exact equivalence/tightness between Subset Sum and OV improvements.
conditional_hypothesis: The upper bounds are unconditional. The 'tight relation' claim is conditional in spirit: IF the OV algorithm is improved THEN Schroeppel-Shamir's Subset Sum runtime improves. Hardness of the OV conjecture is not assumed and gives no lower bound here.
worst_case_vs_average_case_guarantee: Worst-case (the algorithm solves arbitrary worst-case Subset Sum instances). Contrast with the representation-based average-case algorithms.
cryptographic_regime: Subset Sum/knapsack cryptanalysis is an average-case low-density setting; this worst-case result does not break knapsack cryptosystems. (The Schroeppel-Shamir method itself originally had cryptanalytic motivation, breaking knapsack-based systems with up to about n=100 generators.) No samples/density parameters given.
pseudopolynomial_interaction: No direct combination with DP/proximity; the result targets the exponential regime. The OV reduction is orthogonal to pseudopolynomial methods for dense or small-item regimes. [uncertain]
key_references: Jesper Nederlof, Karol Wegrzycki, 'Improving Schroeppel and Shamir's Algorithm for Subset Sum via Orthogonal Vectors', STOC 2021; arXiv:2010.08576 (v2, Apr 2021). https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.08576
Richard Schroeppel, Adi Shamir, 'A T = O(2^{n/2}), S = O(2^{n/4}) Algorithm for Certain NP-Complete Problems', SIAM Journal on Computing 10(3):456-464, 1981. https://doi.org/10.1137/0210033
Tatiana Belova, Nikolai Chukhin, Alexander S. Kulikov, Ivan Mihajlin, 'Improved Space Bounds for Subset Sum', ESA 2024 / arXiv:2402.13170. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13170

Fedor V. Fomin, Daniel Lokshtanov, Fahad Panolan, Saket Saurabh, 'Efficient Computation of Representative Families with Applications in Parameterized and Exact Algorithms', J. ACM 63(4), 2016. https://doi.org/10.1145/2810034
Nick Howgrave-Graham, Antoine Joux, 'New Generic Algorithms for Hard Knapsacks', CRYPTO 2010, LNCS 6110, pp. 235-256. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-14623-7_13

empirical_evidence: None. Purely theoretical upper-bound and reduction result.
verification_method: Reproduce the space-efficient reduction and the support-size d/4 OV algorithm, and verify the representative-families construction and the claimed O~(N * 2^d / binom(d,d/4)) OV running time. The Subset Sum guarantee can be checked by implementing the reduction and Monte Carlo amplification; the tight relation can be verified by plugging an improved OV routine into the reduction.
